::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** October 4th 1859  
**From:** Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS Westcountry Studies Library, Exeter/  Yonge 1859/10[^1]
:::

My dear [Miss Smith](people/person_263.qmd)
I was on a visit in Devonshire when your note reached me, or I would sooner have written to thank you for telling me of the commencement of the printing of [Aggesden Vicarage](other_books/otherbook_268.qmd).  I suppose [Mr Parker](people/person_1143.qmd) intends to have it out in the ‘publishing season’ at Christmas, and I hope it will progress. 

[Frances Dysart](other_books/otherbook_265.qmd) has given unmitigated satisfaction except by coming to an end, everyone likes and admires her, but I am often asked why she has come to an end and have to explain that the author’s rigid truthfulness forbade a pleasant catastrophe.

I like the [Wynnes](other_books/otherbook_267.qmd) much as they proceed, (and so does the [Literary Churchman](organizations/other_76.qmd))[^2]  Those Kelsos are delightful, and enliven the story very much, and we are quite in love with William, but I cannot think what is to become of Henrietta

yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: With envelope addressed to Miss A F C Smith/ Old Charlton Rectory/ S E and postmarked Winchester 4 October and London SE 5 October 1859.
[^2]: ‘Periodicals’ *The Literary Churchman* (16 Sept 1859) 344:  ‘Of the *Churchman’s Companion* after awarding the usual meed of praise to the ‘Wynnes’, we are constrained to say that the September number is a little tame.’
